step1_pipette_pick.goal: Pick up the pipette from the holder on the right with the right hand.
step1_pipette_pick.desc: A humanoid robot reaches the holder on its right, grasps the pipette with the right hand, and lifts it out of the holder.
step1_pipette_pick.steps: step1: reach the holder on the right. step2: grasp the pipette with the right hand. step3: lift the pipette out of the holder.

step2_tube_pick.goal: Pick up the tube from the blue rack on the left with the left hand.
step2_tube_pick.desc: A humanoid robot reaches the blue rack on its left, grasps the sample tube with the left hand, and lifts it out of the rack.
step2_tube_pick.steps: step1: reach the blue rack on the left. step2: grasp the tube with the left hand. step3: lift the tube out of the rack.

step3_pipette_aim_at_tube.goal: Aim the pipette held in the right hand at the tube held in the left hand.
step3_pipette_aim_at_tube.desc: A humanoid robot holds the pipette in its right hand and a sample tube in its left hand, brings the two hands together in front of its body, and aims the pipette tip into the mouth of the tube.
step3_pipette_aim_at_tube.steps: step1: hold the pipette in the right hand and the tube in the left hand. step2: bring the two hands together in front of the body. step3: aim the pipette tip into the mouth of the tube, then move the hands apart again.

step4_tube_return.goal: Put the tube held in the left hand back into the blue rack on the left.
step4_tube_return.desc: A humanoid robot holding a sample tube in its left hand moves it back over the blue rack on its left, lowers it into the rack, and releases it.
step4_tube_return.steps: step1: move the tube over the blue rack on the left. step2: lower the tube into the rack. step3: release the tube and withdraw the hand.

step5_pipette_return.goal: Put the pipette held in the right hand back into the holder on the right.
step5_pipette_return.desc: A humanoid robot holding the pipette in its right hand moves it back over the holder on its right, lowers it into the holder, and releases it.
step5_pipette_return.steps: step1: move the pipette over the holder on the right. step2: lower the pipette into the holder. step3: release the pipette and withdraw the hand.

notes: timestamp is derived from frame_index/fps; the recorder's own per-frame clocks are kept as observation.t_img_ms / observation.t_action_ms.
The recorder's t_state was frozen for every episode and is not carried as a column; its constant value is in source_provenance.jsonl.
Episodes were renumbered across sessions; source_provenance.jsonl maps back.
Video keys mirror the recorder's directory names and are not a claim about camera mounting: measured global frame-to-frame shift shows none of the three pans like a wrist-mounted camera.

episode_splitting.what: each pipette pick-and-return recording became two dataset episodes, pipette_pick (frames [0, cut)) and pipette_return (frames [cut, end)); likewise tube pick-and-return -> tube_pick + tube_return. The two halves are adjacent in the dataset (source_episode names <episode>_pick / <episode>_return in source_provenance.jsonl).
episode_splitting.cut_rule: cut = middle of the plateau where the held object is farthest from where it was grasped: FK of the measured joints for the right (pipette) or left (tube) rubber_hand link; displacement measured from the hand-close frame; smoothed 0.25 s; plateau = >= 90 % of the peak inside the grasp..release window. At the cut the object is raised 6-18 cm above its pick position (median 11 cm), 9-20 cm from it; every cut lies between the grasp and the release, and every half is >= 7 s long.
episode_splitting.tool: VLAPolicyBridge/scripts/dataset/split_recording_episodes.py (builds a split source tree of renumbered symlinks + per-half data.json; the converter then encodes each half as a first-generation video)

teleop_0924_0925.workflow_step_order: task types are numbered as the steps of the full bench workflow, and tasks.jsonl / task_index follow that order: step1 pipette_pick (k=0), step2 tube_pick (k=1), step3 pipette_aim_at_tube (k=2), step4 tube_return (k=3), step5 pipette_return (k=4). Each recording covers ONE step (or a pick/return pair that was split), never the whole chain.

chain_splitting.what: each whole-chain recording became FIVE adjacent dataset episodes, source_episode <episode>_step1 .. _step5 (step k = task type k of the workflow)
chain_splitting.signals: FK of the MEASURED joints (state_body[:29]) for left/right rubber_hand, pelvis frame, smoothed 0.25 s; hand closure = min over the five bend channels of the hand COMMAND (the right closes its four fingers on the pipette, the left its THUMB on the tube); grasp = first frame below 500, release = the frame after the last frame below 500

cut_rule.c1 (pipette pick | tube pick): (revised after operator review, release v1.2) the pipette FULLY OUT of its holder and the right hand moving toward the middle: the first frame where the right hand is >= 11 cm above AND >= 2 cm toward the middle (+y) of where it grasped the pipette, no later than 1 s after it first reaches 11 cm (4 takes where the right hand waits for the left); one reviewed override (1345/episode_0016: the pipette slipped in the grasp, so the 11 cm rise came before the tip left the holder)
cut_rule.c2 (tube pick | aim): the same rule on the LEFT hand inside [left grasp, approach onset]; approach onset = hand distance 4 cm below its value at the left grasp
cut_rule.c3 (aim | tube return): the hands apart again: first frame after the closest-approach plateau (<= minimum + 2 cm) whose distance is back at its value at c2
cut_rule.c4 (tube return | pipette return): right onset after the tube release (right hand 2 cm from where it was at the release), >= 0.5 s after the release

chain_splitting.result: 30 recordings, no flags; phase lengths median 10.6 / 7.1 / 6.0 / 8.4 / 8.7 s (shortest 4.8 s); pipette 14.3 cm (11.9-17.3) above its grasp height at c1, the right hand 2.1 cm toward the middle (median); tube 8 cm (5.4-11) at c2; closest approach 26-31 cm; every cut frame checked on head-camera contact sheets, c1 reviewed by the operator

c1_revision.when: 2026-10-07, after operator review of the first release (HF tag v1.1-447eps)
c1_revision.why: the first rule cut most takes while the pipette was still in or just at the top of its holder (and 3 takes after the right hand had crossed to the middle); the operator's boundary is the pipette fully out and the right hand starting toward the middle
c1_revision.effect: 27 cuts later, 3 earlier (median +1.0 s, -0.5..+3.6 s); only the step1 / step2 episodes of the 30 chains changed (frames move between the two, totals unchanged)
